claims.explanation: Triptolide covalently inhibits XPB/ERCC3, a TFIIH subunit required for RNA polymerase II transcription and nucleotide excision repair, causing rapid RNAPII degradation and transcriptional arrest. Selectivity likely reflects dependence on high transcriptional output and intact DNA-repair/transcription-coupled repair capacity, so tumors with high ERCC3/XPB expression and intact NER, plus those reliant on NF-kB/RELA-driven survival, are most sensitive, while low ERCC3 or high apoptosis resistance (e.g., BCL2/MCL1) protects.

features.basis: XPB/ERCC3 is the direct covalent target of triptolide; higher target expression increases drug engagement and transcriptional arrest
annotated target; NF-kB/RELA-dependent survival signaling is inhibited by triptolide
TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set, consistent with loss of p53-mediated survival/repair responses after transcriptional stress
anti-apoptotic BCL2 overexpression blunts apoptosis induction triggered by transcriptional inhibition
MCL1 is a key anti-apoptotic resistance factor against apoptosis-inducing anticancer therapies
loss of caspase-mediated apoptosis signaling reduces sensitivity to apoptosis-inducing drugs
caspase pathway inactivation contributes to chemoresistance
virtual cell shows NFKBIA downregulation; low NFKBIA would sustain NF-kB survival signaling and reduce triptolide effect
CDKN2A loss appears in several sensitive lines and may impair cell-cycle checkpoint arrest after transcriptional stress
ARID1A mutations recur in sensitive lines, suggesting SWI/SNF-dependent transcriptional dependencies
BRAF-mutant melanoma and other lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly reflecting MAPK-driven transcriptional addiction
SMARCA4-mutant lines appear among least-affected lines, suggesting SWI/SNF loss alters transcriptional dependency
